K1.stone_why: Faceted, chiselled bold weights and the wedge-cut caps read convincingly as hewn letters while the regular stays grounded.
K1.carving_why: The cuts are angular and deliberate and shared by caps, lowercase and digits, though the bold 62.5 looks slightly rough beside the smooth regular 147.5.
K1.calm_why: It has strong presence in bold without shouting, and the regular weights are steady.
K1.personality_why: The faceted bold and the heavy cut SISIFO give it a recognisable voice.
K1.inscription_why: The ss01 caps are wide and dignified with round O and C, close to Roman proportions, though the heavy bold SISIFO leans more poster than lapidary.

K2.stone_why: It has the same faceted chiselled bold, and the carved caps feel cut into stone.
K2.carving_why: Cuts are coherent across caps, lowercase and digits, and the digits are clearly distinct.
K2.calm_why: It is calm and present, though the condensed caps add some vertical tension.
K2.personality_why: The carved facets are distinctive, but the condensed caps make it read more like a generic condensed titling face.
K2.inscription_why: The ss01 caps are narrow and condensed, so O, C and D are not wide and the rhythm is far from classical Roman proportions.

K3.stone_why: The all-caps Trajan/Cinzel-like design evokes inscriptions, but its smooth flared strokes show no hewn quality.
K3.carving_why: No visible carving or faceting; the strokes are smooth, and the ss01 swash ligatures (LI, long R and Q tails) look decorative rather than cut.
K3.calm_why: The regular is elegant, but the ornate swashes and the caps-only body text are busy and theatrical rather than calm.
K3.personality_why: It is very recognisable, though the character is borrowed classical-display flourish more than a voice of its own.
K3.inscription_why: The base caps have Roman proportions, but the ss01 swash ligatures move it toward calligraphic display rather than stone cutting.

K4.stone_why: Its chiselled bold faceting and cut caps read as hewn stone while staying controlled.
K4.carving_why: Crisp, consistent cuts across caps, lowercase and digits, and the caps feel part of the same design, though the carved bold digits sit beside an uncarved regular set.
K4.calm_why: Bold presence with a measured rhythm; nothing feels aggressive.
K4.personality_why: The faceted bold with its classical caps (including the long-tailed Q) has a recognisable character.
K4.inscription_why: The ss01 caps are wide-round and lighter than K1's, with a classical Q tail and a dignified rhythm close to Roman inscription.

K5.stone_why: A clean, smooth bookish serif with no hewn or carved quality.
K5.carving_why: There is no visible carving; the bold is smooth throughout.
K5.calm_why: Very calm and steady with good presence in bold.
K5.personality_why: A competent but anonymous text serif.
K5.inscription_why: The ss01 caps are condensed and narrow, lacking wide round O, C and D, so they do not read as Roman lettering.
